one_line: Nvidia investigates its CEO over a spy link, AI companies face market and energy demands, and new safety policies emerge.

themes.title: Nvidia investigates CEO over spy link
themes.text: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with an executive whom U.S. officials allege is a Chinese spy. The board stated there is no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

stories.headline: Nvidia board launches investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admits affair
Nvidia board launches probe into CEO Jensen Huang over alleged spy plot
Nvidia board investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair with alleged Chinese spy

themes.title: AI infrastructure spending and market shifts
themes.text: Anthropic purchased 1.7GW of gas-fired generators for $3.4 billion, while AI companies sold over $300 billion in stock amid market absorption questions. Meanwhile, Envision Group opened a gigawatt-scale AI datacenter in Inner Mongolia and ByteDance considered expanding a project in Brazil.

stories.headline: Anthropic buys 1.7GW of gas-fired generators in $3.4B deal
Envision Group opens gigawatt-scale Galaxy AI datacenter in Inner Mongolia
AI companies sell $300B+ in stock in 2026 amid market absorption questions
ByteDance considers data center expansion in Ceará, Brazil

themes.title: New AI regulations and lawsuits
themes.text: India's CERT-In issued security auditing guidelines for autonomous AI systems, and rights holders for Elvis and Eminem filed copyright lawsuits against Suno. Additionally, US officials at the CAISSI safety center were asked to informally report to the White House.

stories.headline: CERT-In issues AI security auditing guidelines for autonomous systems
Elvis and Eminem rights holders file lawsuits against AI music platform Suno
US AI safety center officials asked to informally report to White House
